name: Fridge Cigarette
description: Cold Diet Coke, bold espresso and a silky vanilla cloud. Fizzy, creamy, unexpected.
ingredients: Ice, to fill the serving glass
For the vanilla cloud: 30 ml whipping cream
For the vanilla cloud: 10 ml milk
For the vanilla cloud: 10 ml vanilla syrup
steps: Pull one double-shot espresso; allow it to settle briefly while you prepare the glass.
Whisk or froth the 30 ml whipping cream, 10 ml milk and 10 ml vanilla syrup into a soft, pourable vanilla cloud.
Add ice to a tall serving glass.
Pour 100–120 ml chilled Diet Coke over the ice.
Slowly pour the double-shot espresso over the cola to preserve the layers and limit foaming.
Gently spoon or pour the vanilla cloud on top, and serve immediately.
notes: Pour slowly: cola can foam when espresso is added. The vanilla syrup already sweetens the cloud.

name: Classic Affogato
description: Cold vanilla ice cream melting into a freshly pulled double espresso, finished with cocoa.
ingredients: A light dusting of chocolate powder or unsweetened cocoa powder
steps: Scoop 120–130 ml vanilla ice cream into a chilled dessert bowl or small glass.
Pull one fresh double-shot espresso using your espresso machine.
Pour the hot espresso directly over the ice cream just before serving.
Finish with a light dusting of chocolate powder or cocoa. Enjoy immediately.
notes: Serve immediately for the contrast between hot espresso and cold ice cream.

name: Salted Caramel Affogato
description: Classic vanilla affogato with a generous caramel ribbon and a tiny pinch of salt.
steps: Scoop 120–130 ml vanilla ice cream into a chilled dessert bowl or glass.
Drizzle 20 g caramel sauce over the ice cream.
Pull one fresh double-shot espresso and pour it over the dessert.
Finish with a tiny pinch of salt to make it a salted caramel affogato. Serve immediately.
notes: Use only a small pinch of salt; caramel sauce is already sweet.

name: Jamun Coffee Tonic
description: Muddled jamun, lime and sparkling tonic meet a fresh double espresso.
ingredients: Ice, to fill a 300 ml glass
steps: Deseed 40–50 g ripe jamun and gently muddle it in the serving glass with 5 ml lime juice and a tiny pinch of salt.
Fill the glass with ice.
Slowly add 120–130 ml chilled tonic water.
Pull a fresh double-shot espresso and let it settle briefly.
Gently pour the espresso over the back of a spoon to create a layered finish; serve immediately.
notes: Adjust tonic slightly for your actual shot yield and the amount of ice in your glass.

name: Sunrise Americano
description: Fresh orange, soda and espresso in a bright, sparkling sunrise of a glass.
steps: Fill a serving glass with ice.
Pour in 80 ml chilled orange juice.
Add 60 ml chilled soda water slowly.
Pull a double-shot espresso and slowly pour it over the drink for a layered sunrise effect.
Garnish with a fresh orange slice and serve immediately.
notes: Use cold juice and soda for clearer layers; espresso should be poured slowly.

name: Sunset Americano
description: A vivid layered americano with cranberry, orange, soda and a double espresso finish.
steps: Fill a serving glass with ice.
Pour 60 ml chilled cranberry juice over the ice.
Add 50 ml chilled orange juice.
Slowly pour in 50 ml chilled soda water.
Pull one fresh double-shot espresso and gently pour it on top as the final layer.
Garnish with a fresh orange slice and serve immediately.
notes: Keep each ingredient well chilled for cleaner layers. The order matters: ice → cranberry → orange → soda → espresso.

name: Dark Chocolate Peanut Butter Iced Latte
description: Chocolate milk, honey-kissed peanut butter espresso and a fluffy honey cloud.
ingredients: 2–3 g Hershey’s chocolate powder, to make chocolate milk
8–10 g honey, for the espresso mixture
For the honey cloud: 30 ml whipping cream
For the honey cloud: 10 ml milk
For the honey cloud: 10 ml honey
Chocolate or cocoa powder, for dusting
steps: Prepare chocolate milk by mixing 2–3 g Hershey’s chocolate powder smoothly into 120 ml chilled milk (make a paste with a small splash of the milk first if needed).
Pull one double-shot espresso. While warm, thoroughly stir in 1 tbsp dark chocolate peanut butter and 8–10 g honey until as smooth as possible.
Pour the chocolate milk into a tall glass, then add ice.
Slowly pour the peanut-butter-and-honey espresso over the ice.
Whisk or froth 30 ml whipping cream, 10 ml milk and 10 ml honey until thick yet pourable.
Spoon the honey cloud on top and finish with a light chocolate or cocoa dusting.
notes: Contains peanuts and dairy. Stir peanut butter thoroughly into hot espresso before pouring; cloud toppings are best made fresh.

name: Hot Cappuccino
description: A comforting double espresso topped with velvety steamed milk and soft foam, sweetened exactly how you like.
ingredients: Optional sweetener: brown sugar, honey, condensed milk, white sugar or stevia (amount to taste)
steps: Pull one freshly brewed double-shot espresso into a pre-warmed cappuccino cup.
If requested, add the guest’s chosen sweetener to the espresso and stir until incorporated. Start with a small amount and adjust to taste.
Steam and texture 180–200 g milk until silky, with fine microfoam suitable for a cappuccino.
Pour the steamed milk gently into the espresso, finishing with a soft foam layer and latte art if desired.
Serve immediately while hot.
notes: Sweetener is optional. Guests select their preferred type when ordering; quantities are adjustable to taste. The requested 180–200 g milk gives a larger, milk-forward cappuccino.

name: Salted Caramel Iced Latte
serve: Iced latte · 120 g milk + caramel cloud
description: Medium-dark espresso whipped with caramel, chilled milk and a soft salted-caramel cloud.
brewMethod: Espresso machine · double shot (36–40 g yield)
ingredients: 1 double-shot espresso (36–40 g liquid yield), using medium-dark roast beans
13–15 g Hershey’s caramel sauce (less sweet), or 20–22 g (sweeter), for the espresso
For the caramel cloud: 25–30 ml whipping cream
For the caramel cloud: 10 ml milk
For the caramel cloud: 6–7 ml caramel sauce
For the caramel cloud: a small pinch of salt
steps: Pull a double-shot espresso from medium-dark roast beans, targeting 36–40 g of liquid espresso.
Add 13–15 g Hershey’s caramel sauce for a less-sweet latte, or 20–22 g for a sweeter version, to the main serving glass.
Pour the hot espresso into that glass and blend the caramel and espresso thoroughly using a handheld frother until smooth.
Add ice to the caramel-espresso mixture.
Pour in 120 g chilled milk.
In a separate pitcher, whisk or froth 25–30 ml whipping cream, 10 ml milk, 6–7 ml caramel sauce and a small pinch of salt into a soft, pourable caramel cloud.
Gently spoon or pour the salted caramel cloud over the latte and serve immediately.
notes: The 36–40 g refers to brewed espresso yield, not the dry coffee dose. Caramel quantities for the main drink are chosen by the guest; the cloud uses an additional 6–7 ml caramel sauce. Mix caramel with hot espresso before adding ice.

name: Hot Americano
description: Clean, aromatic black coffee made your way: strong, balanced or light.
ingredients: 1 freshly pulled double-shot espresso (32 g liquid yield in these examples)
Strong (1:2 espresso-to-water): 64 g hot water for 32 g espresso
Balanced / mild (1:3): 96 g hot water for 32 g espresso
Light (1:4): 128 g hot water for 32 g espresso
steps: Preheat a serving cup with hot water, then empty it.
Pull one double-shot espresso using your espresso machine. Weigh the liquid yield (32 g in the example).
Choose your strength: Strong uses 2 parts hot water per part espresso; Balanced uses 3; Light uses 4.
For a 32 g espresso yield, measure 64 g hot water (Strong), 96 g (Balanced) or 128 g (Light).
Pour the chosen hot-water amount into the cup, add the double-shot espresso, and serve immediately.
notes: Ratios are espresso yield : added hot water by weight. If your double-shot yield is different, multiply the espresso yield by 2, 3 or 4. For example, a 36 g shot uses 72 g, 108 g or 144 g hot water.
orderPreferences: Strong · 1:2 (32 g espresso + 64 g hot water)
Balanced / mild · 1:3 (32 g espresso + 96 g hot water)
Light · 1:4 (32 g espresso + 128 g hot water)

name: Iced Americano
description: Crisp, refreshing espresso over ice, tailored from bold to easy-sipping.
ingredients: 1 freshly pulled double-shot espresso (32 g liquid yield in these examples)
60–80 g ice, for all three versions
Balanced / mild: 75 g chilled water (your preferred recipe)
steps: Pull one double-shot espresso, targeting a 32 g liquid yield.
Weigh 60–80 g ice into a serving glass.
For a strong iced Americano, add 50 g chilled water; for balanced / mild, add 75 g; for light, add 100 g.
Slowly pour the freshly pulled espresso over the ice and water.
Stir lightly and serve straight away. Add or reduce chilled water to suit the actual ice melt.
notes: These are iced, melt-adjusted starting measurements based on your balanced standard of 32 g espresso + 75 g water + 60–80 g ice. Strong (50 g) and Light (100 g) scale around that baseline. Because melting ice adds water, these are NOT exact 1:2, 1:3 and 1:4 espresso-to-added-water ratios like the hot versions.
orderPreferences: Strong · 32 g espresso + 50 g chilled water + 60–80 g ice
Balanced / mild · 32 g espresso + 75 g chilled water + 60–80 g ice
Light · 32 g espresso + 100 g chilled water + 60–80 g ice
